statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, define D = { d | 0 <= d <= 9 and there exists i with 0 <= i < len(s) and s[i] = 48 + d }, the set of distinct numerical digit values occurring in s. Then: if D has fewer than two elements, r = -1; if D has at least two elements, r = max { d | d in D and d < max D }, i.e. r is the largest digit value occurring in s that is strictly smaller than the largest digit value occurring in s. Equivalently, r is -1 when fewer than two distinct digit values occur, and otherwise r is the second largest distinct digit value occurring in s.
preconditions: Let len(s) be the number of bytes of s. Assume 1 <= len(s) <= 500, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), the byte s[i] is either an ASCII digit byte (48 <= s[i] <= 57) or a lowercase English letter byte (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, the set of numerical digit values d occurring in s with d > r has exactly one element. A digit value d occurs in s iff there is an index i with 0 <= i < len(s) and s[i] = 48 + d.
preconditions: Let len(s) be the number of bytes of s. Assume 1 <= len(s) <= 500, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), the byte s[i] is either an ASCII digit byte (48 <= s[i] <= 57) or a lowercase English letter byte (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: For any such t, if the set of distinct numerical digit values occurring in s equals the set of distinct numerical digit values occurring in t (d occurs in s iff d occurs in t, where d occurs in a slice iff some byte equals 48 + d), then whenever second_highest(s) returns r and second_highest(t) returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let len(s) and len(t) be the numbers of bytes. Assume 1 <= len(s) <= 500, 1 <= len(t) <= 500, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is an ASCII digit byte (48 <= s[i] <= 57) or a lowercase English letter byte (97 <= s[i] <= 122); and similarly for every i with 0 <= i < len(t).
